title: White Rice with Carrots and Dark Green Vegetables, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: A ready‑to‑eat dish made from boiled white rice, carrots and dark green vegetables (such as broccoli or spinach), prepared with a small amount of added vegetable fat. It has a mild flavor, a hint of sweetness from the carrots, and the fresh taste of the greens.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The combination of white rice and carrots is a staple in many Asian and Eastern European cuisines.
Dark green vegetables are rich in chlorophyll, giving them their vivid color and distinctive flavor.
Adding a little fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins from the vegetables.
The dish is often served in school cafeterias as a source of energy and vitamins for children.
When stored properly, it stays fresh for up to 3 days in the refrigerator.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides quick‑digesting carbohydrates, while the added fat raises the calorie content, useful for active individuals.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both rice and carrots contain B1, B3 and B6 vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Beta‑carotene
items.content: Carrots are high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A for eye health.

items.title: Antioxidants from greens
items.content: Dark green vegetables supply lutein and zeaxanthin, protecting the eyes from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: The added vegetable fat helps the body absorb vitamins A, D, E and K found in the greens.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of the added fat, the dish can be calorie‑dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: Some individuals may react to the type of oil used (e.g., sunflower or olive oil).

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: If seasoned with salt, sodium intake should be monitored, especially for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a standalone meal or as a side dish with meat, fish, or tofu. It reheats well in the microwave or on the stovetop; add a splash of water to prevent drying out.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months.
